advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the 'CI drift gate' language in docs/config-reference.md, docs/security.md, and the docs/README.md table with the actual enforcement mechanism (a make-test unit test), or add the named CI gate the docs promise.
evidence: docs/config-reference.md banner: 'a CI drift gate fails the build if this file is stale'
docs/README.md table row: '| `docs/config-reference.md` | ... | Config-reference drift gate |'
commit message: 'A newline-normalized --check mode, gated by tests/unit/test_gen_config_reference.py under make test, fails on drift without a CI dependency.'

Sibling generators (gen_env_registry.py) reference an actual 'Env-var registry drift gate' CI job; this generator's drift check is a unit test, so 'CI gate' terminology is inconsistent with its actual wiring.
advisory.finding: The generated docs, their banners, and the docs/README.md generated-surface table all describe enforcement as a 'CI drift gate' ('kept in sync by a CI drift gate', 'a CI drift gate fails the build', 'Enforcing CI gate: Config-reference drift gate'), but the commit message states the mechanism is a `make test` unit test 'without a CI dependency'. The enforcement is pytest (tests/unit/test_gen_config_reference.py), not a dedicated named CI gate like the sibling generators — the doc language overstates/mischaracterizes the enforcement surface.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the docstring of tests/unit/test_gen_config_reference.py so it matches the fact that the edge/E2E oracle is present in this file, not held out.
evidence: Docstring: 'The edge/E2E oracle (config.md preservation, lifecycle column, secret inventory, topic coverage, CRLF newline-safety, drift-trips) is held out in a separate suite the implementer never sees.'

Same file then defines test_generator_never_writes_config_md, test_config_reference_reflects_cfg_tombstones, test_security_doc_lists_every_adapter_secret_name, test_check_is_crlf_safe, etc. under '# ── EDGE CASES (HELD OUT) ──'.
advisory.finding: tests/unit/test_gen_config_reference.py claims in its docstring that the edge/E2E oracle 'is held out in a separate suite the implementer never sees', yet the same file inlines all of those held-out tests (config.md preservation, lifecycle column, secret inventory, topic coverage, CRLF safety, drift trips) under an 'EDGE CASES (HELD OUT)' comment. The docstring contract and the file contents contradict each other.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Isolate the drift/CRLF tests from the real committed docs (e.g. monkeypatch the output paths to tmp_path) so a failed run cannot leave tracked docs dirty.
evidence: test_check_trips_on_a_stale_doc: 'CONFIG_REFERENCE.write_text(original + "\n<!-- drift -->\n", ...)' then restores in finally.
test_regenerate_writes_both_docs / test_check_trips call 'gen.main([])' which does 'CONFIG_REFERENCE_PATH.write_text(...)' against the real repo path, not a tmp fixture.
tmp_path/monkeypatch are declared as params of test_check_trips_on_a_stale_doc but never used.
test_check_trips_on_a_stale_doc writes only `CONFIG_REFERENCE.write_text(original + "\n<!-- drift -->\n", ...)` and asserts `gen.main(["--check"]) != 0`
search for `SECURITY.write` in the test file returns `(no matches)` — SECURITY is only ever read, never mutated to force a drift
main()'s --check loop iterates over BOTH (CONFIG_REFERENCE_PATH, config_doc) and (SECURITY_PATH, security_doc) in scripts/gen_config_reference.py, but only the config-reference half is proven to trip
advisory.finding: test_check_trips_on_a_stale_doc and test_check_is_crlf_safe mutate the committed docs/config-reference.md on disk and rely on a try/finally to restore it; if the process is interrupted between write and restore (or the restore write itself fails), the committed doc is left in a drifted/CRLF state, and these tests also have an order dependency (they call gen.main([]) which overwrites the real committed files rather than a tmp copy).
merged_from: Drift detection for docs/security.md is never exercised: the drift-trip test mutates only docs/config-reference.md, so a regression where --check fails to detect a stale security.md would pass all tests.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Redirect the generator's output paths to tmp_path (monkeypatch CONFIG_REFERENCE_PATH/SECURITY_PATH) so tests never write to the committed docs.
evidence: test_regenerate_writes_both_docs: `assert gen.main([]) == 0` — main() calls `CONFIG_REFERENCE_PATH.write_text(...)` and `SECURITY_PATH.write_text(...)` against the repo tree, with no teardown restoring prior content
test_generator_never_writes_config_md and test_check_trips_on_a_stale_doc/test_check_is_crlf_safe also invoke gen.main([]) / CONFIG_REFERENCE.write_* on the real committed files
tmp_path/monkeypatch are accepted by test_check_trips_on_a_stale_doc but never used to redirect the output paths
advisory.finding: Several tests mutate the REAL committed working-tree docs instead of a temp copy; test_regenerate_writes_both_docs and test_generator_never_writes_config_md call gen.main([]) (which overwrites docs/config-reference.md and docs/security.md) with no restore, leaving the tree dirty and creating cross-test/order dependence and a filesystem-state leak.
scenarios: Docs are stale in the tree; gen.main([]) regenerates them mid-suite, masking the drift the gate exists to catch
A test aborts before its finally block, or an unguarded main([]) run leaves docs/config-reference.md modified for subsequent tests and for the developer's working tree
advisory.suggested_fix: Monkeypatch gen.CONFIG_REFERENCE_PATH and gen.SECURITY_PATH to files under tmp_path in a fixture, then run main([])/main(['--check']) against those copies instead of the committed tree.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert the rendered lifecycle status text ('permanent alias' or 'deprecated (removal in <ver>)') and its placement in the Lifecycle column, not just name/replacement presence.
evidence: test_config_reference_reflects_cfg_deprecation_aliases: `assert dep.name in doc` and `assert dep.replacement in doc` — only substring presence anywhere in the document

_cfg_deprecations() computes `status = 'permanent alias' if dep.permanent else f'deprecated (removal in {dep.remove_in})'` in scripts/gen_config_reference.py, and _lifecycle_index() renders `active — supersedes alias ... ({status})`, none of which any assertion checks
the non-permanent (remove_in) status branch has no cfg fixture that would exercise it and no assertion on its text
advisory.finding: The lifecycle-column tests assert the deprecated key name and its replacement appear somewhere in the doc, but never assert the rendered lifecycle STATUS string ('permanent alias' / 'deprecated (removal in <ver>)') nor that they land in the Lifecycle column, so the status-branch logic in _cfg_deprecations/_lifecycle_index is unverified.
scenarios: A bug in the permanent/remove_in status formatting or the lifecycle-column composition ships without a test failing
A non-permanent cfg deprecation is added and its 'removal in <ver>' status renders incorrectly
advisory.suggested_fix: For each cfg deprecation, assert the expected status string from _cfg_deprecations appears in the doc and that the canonical replacement row's Lifecycle cell contains 'supersedes alias `<name>`'.
